message.abstract:
<jats:p><jats:italic>Context.</jats:italic> Fast X-ray transients (FXTs) are a rare and poorly understood phenomenon with a variety of possible progenitors. The launch of the <jats:italic>Einstein Probe</jats:italic> (EP) mission has facilitated a rapid increase in the real-time discovery and follow-up of FXTs.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Aims.</jats:italic> We focus on the recent EP discovered transient EP241021a, which shows a peculiar panchromatic behavior, with the aim of understanding its origin.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Methods.</jats:italic> We obtained optical and near-infrared multiband imaging and spectroscopy with the Fraunhofer Telescope at Wendelstein Observatory, the Hobby-Eberly Telescope, and the Very Large Telescope of the newly discovered EP transient EP241021a over the first 100 days of its evolution.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Results.</jats:italic> EP241021a was discovered by EP as a soft X-ray trigger, but was not detected at gamma-ray frequencies. The observed soft X-ray prompt emission spectrum is consistent with nonthermal radiation, which requires at least a mildly relativistic outflow with a bulk Lorentz factor Γ ≳ 4. The optical and near-infrared light curve displays a two-component behavior, where an initially fading component, ∼ <jats:italic>t</jats:italic><jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>, transitions to a rise steeper than ∼ <jats:italic>t</jats:italic><jats:sup>3</jats:sup> after a few days, before peaking at an absolute magnitude of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>r</jats:italic></jats:sub> ≈ −21.8 mag and quickly returning to the initial decay. Standard supernova models are unable to reproduce either the absolute magnitude or the rapid timescale (< 2 d) of the rebrightening. The X-ray, optical and near-infrared spectral energy distributions display a red color, <jats:italic>r</jats:italic> − <jats:italic>J</jats:italic> ≈ 0.8 mag, and point to a nonthermal origin (∼ <jats:italic>ν</jats:italic><jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>) for the broadband emission. Considering a gamma-ray burst as a plausible scenario, we favor a refreshed shock as the cause of the rebrightening. This is consistent with the inference of an at least mildly relativistic outflow based on the prompt trigger.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Conclusions.</jats:italic> Our results suggest a link between EP-discovered FXTs and gamma-ray bursts, despite the lack of gamma-ray detections for the majority of EP transients.</jats:p>
title: The curious case of EP241021a: Unraveling the mystery of its exceptional rebrightening
